app.name: Ferrule
app.tagline: One local panel: every key held once, every model — local or cloud — visible, switchable, and accountable for what leaves your machine.
app.sovereignty: Your keys are persisted locally and encrypted. That is not the same as persisted on someone's server. Ferrule has no account, sends no telemetry, and never transmits a key anywhere but the provider you gave it for. The one request Ferrule makes on its own behalf is a background fetch of the public model-capability catalog; it carries nothing about you, and you can turn it off.
cli.usage: ferrule — a local key vault and model router
cli.usage.verbs:
Verbs:
  status   the whole situation in one read (--json for an agent)
  serve    start the daemon (endpoints + control surface)
  add      add a source (paste a key, or adopt a detected runtime)
  ls       list sources / models / aliases
  alias    create, edit, or remove an alias
  remap    serve a hardcoded model id from a model of your choosing
  key      mint or revoke an app token
  usage    per-app and per-model spend, volume, and egress
  export   write a portable encrypted configuration file
  import   read a portable encrypted configuration file
  version  print the version

Exit codes: 0 the thing worked · 1 it did not, and the reason says why · 2 the
command was wrong.

op.list_sources: List every source, live and failed, with its reason.
op.list_models: List every model on every live source, with capability, context, and cost.
op.list_aliases: List every alias and its fallback ladder.
op.get_alias: Read one alias and its fallback ladder.
op.set_alias: Point an alias at an ordered ladder of models.
op.set_remap: Serve a hardcoded model id from a model of your choosing.
op.add_source: Add a source: paste a key for a known provider, or a key and base URL for an unknown OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
op.remove_source: Remove a source, its models, and its stored key.
op.refresh_source: Re-probe a source and re-classify its models.
op.detect_local: Scan localhost for known runtimes and adopt what is running.
op.usage_summary: Spend, volume, latency, and errors, grouped as you ask.
op.egress_summary: What left the machine, and what stayed on it.
op.list_grants: List app tokens and what each one spent.
op.mint_grant: Mint an app token. Person-only: it returns a credential, shown once.
op.list_staged: List control operations staged for a person to apply.
op.status: Ferrule's own state: version, config dir, vault backend, catalog date.
op.export_config: Write a portable encrypted configuration file, sealed under a passphrase so the file alone is the whole configuration. Person-only: it writes your keys to a path you choose.
op.import_config: Read a portable encrypted configuration file and merge it into local state — sources, models, aliases, remaps and app tokens are added or updated, and nothing local is deleted. Person-only: it writes keys into your vault.
app.tagline-short: a local key vault and model router
ui.add.name: Name
ui.add.testing: Probing, classifying, and firing one real request
ui.add.body: Paste a key. Ferrule probes the endpoint, classifies what it finds, and fires one minimal real request before it calls the source live. A key that does not work is never quietly stored.
ui.add.failHint: The source is kept as failed with the reason above. Fix the key or the URL and add it again.
ui.add.detectBody: Ferrule scans localhost at start and adopts what is running. It never downloads a model uninvited.
ui.alias.name: Name
ui.alias.ladderHint: Rungs are tried in order. The first reachable one serves; a dead rung is stepped over, not raised as an error.
ui.alias.emptyBody: An alias is a name your apps point at — fast, cheap, local — backed by an ordered ladder you re-point here, with nothing to restart.
ui.board.emptyHint: Add a cloud provider with a key, or start a local runtime and rescan.
ui.confirm.removeSourceBody: This deletes the source, its classified models, and its stored key. Aliases pointing at it will step over the dead rung.
ui.egress.title: What left this machine
ui.egress.body: Every request Ferrule routed, split by whether it stayed on the machine or went to a provider. Metadata only — prompts and responses are not recorded.
ui.grants.body: Each app gets its own token. The token is the app's identity to Ferrule — never a provider key — and it is what makes per-app spend and egress possible.
ui.grants.emptyBody: Mint one per app or script. Point it at this daemon and its calls show up attributed.
ui.help.title: Keys
ui.help.body: Press a number to switch section. Everything on this panel is also a CLI verb and an MCP control op — one command bus, three doors.
ui.remap.title: Model remapping
ui.remap.body: For an app that will only ever send one model id. Intercept it here and serve it from whatever you choose, including a local model.
ui.sovereignty.title: Where your keys live
ui.staged.body: An agent asked for these changes through the MCP control face. Mutating operations never land on their own — you apply them.
ui.staged.secretPlaceholder: the key was withheld from staging — paste it now
ui.usage.emptyHint: Point an app at Ferrule with an app token and its calls show up here, per app and per model.
op.read_content: Read the local content log, when content logging is on. Person-only: it returns prompt and response text.
op.forget_content: Delete everything the content log holds.
content.off: Content logging is off. Nothing was recorded.
content.empty: Content logging is on, but nothing has been recorded yet.
ui.sov.contentOn: Local content logging is ON. Prompts and responses are being written to this machine's disk.
ui.sov.contentOff: Local content logging is off. Only metadata is recorded — no prompt or response text.
remedy.unreachable: Check the base URL, and that the service is running and listening.
remedy.bad_key: Mint a fresh key with the provider and add the source again.
remedy.bad_status: Read the provider's message above; it is theirs, not Ferrule's.
remedy.no_models: Confirm the base URL points at an OpenAI-compatible /v1 root.
reason.local_no_models: %s is running but has no models installed
remedy.local_no_models: Pull a model in that runtime, then rescan. Ferrule never downloads anything uninvited.
remedy.test_failed: The source listed models but would not serve one. Check the key's scope and the provider's status.
remedy.unknown_provider: Known providers: %s. Or use `openai-compatible` with --base-url for anything else that speaks the OpenAI API.
remedy.needs_key: Pass --key, or leave it out to be prompted without echo.
reason.needs_base_url: an unknown OpenAI-compatible source needs a base URL
remedy.needs_base_url: Pass --base-url pointing at the endpoint's /v1 root.
op.brief: The whole situation in one bounded read: sources and why any are dark, what the router can serve, aliases and their live rung, spend and egress, what is staged, and what to do next.
next.addSource: No source is live. Add one: `ferrule add` to adopt a local runtime, or `ferrule add <provider>` to paste a key.
next.mintGrant: No app token exists. Mint one with `ferrule key <app>` and point your app at %s.
next.setAlias: No alias is defined. `ferrule alias fast <source>/<model>` gives your apps a name you can re-point without restarting them.
next.applyStaged: %d control operation(s) staged by an agent are waiting for you to apply or discard.
next.catalogStale: The capability catalog has not refreshed in over a day. Costs and context lengths may be behind.
cli.status.title: ferrule %s · %s
next.reprobe: Re-probe it with `ferrule add` or the Refresh button to get a typed reason.
reason.test_timeout: the test request timed out after %s
remedy.test_timeout: A local runtime does this while it loads a model into memory. Wait a moment and add it again; the second attempt is quick.
remedy.test_failed_local: The runtime listed models but would not serve one. Check its own logs.
step.test: firing one real request to be sure it serves…
step.testLocal: firing one real request to be sure it serves — a local runtime may need to load the model first, which can take a minute on a cold start…
ui.board.detectingBody: Ferrule is firing one real request at each runtime it found, to be sure it serves. A local runtime may need to load a model first, which can take a minute on a cold start.
passthrough.wrongLane: %s is a raw-tokens source. Its key is not reachable through the passthrough mount — call it at /v1 instead.
reason.insecure_url: %s is not a loopback address, so it must be https — a key sent over http is a key sent in the clear
remedy.insecure_url: Use an https base URL, or point at a runtime on this machine. If this really is a trusted network you control, add the source again with --insecure and Ferrule will mark it as such.
reason.redirect: the endpoint redirected to %s; Ferrule does not follow redirects when a key is attached
remedy.redirect: Point the base URL at the endpoint the provider actually serves, with no redirect in front of it.
vault.busy: another Ferrule process is holding the vault; try again in a moment
route.remapDark: %q is remapped to %q, which is not reachable
route.truncated: the response was not delivered whole: %s
catalog.disclosure: Ferrule fetches the model capability catalog from %s in the background so costs and context lengths stay current. That request carries no information about you — no key, no prompt, no identifier — but it is a request to a third party, and you can turn it off with `catalog_refresh off`, in which case the bundled snapshot is used.
op.catalog_refresh: Refresh the capability catalog from its maintained source now.
serve.catalogOff: Catalog refresh is off; using the bundled snapshot from %s.
export.needPassphrase: an export needs a passphrase of at least 8 characters — it is what seals your keys inside the file
route.redirectRefused: %s redirected to %s; Ferrule does not follow a redirect while carrying your key
serve.controlBindRefused:
Refusing to serve the control surface on %s.

The panel carries this run's control token in the page it is served, and the MCP door has no auth of its own — both are safe only because nothing but this machine can reach them. Binding them to a routable address hands administrative control of your keys to the network.

Use --host 127.0.0.1 (the default). If you need the inference endpoints reachable from elsewhere, put a reverse proxy you control in front of /v1 and /p and leave the control surface here.
ui.egress.meterLabel: Share of requests that stayed on this machine: %s%%
passthrough.methodRefused: %s is not an inference call on %s. The passthrough mount carries your provider key, so it serves that provider's inference surface and nothing else — account, billing, and file operations are yours to make directly.
reason.credential_in_url: the base URL carries a credential in its %s
remedy.credential_in_url: Put the key in the key field. A base URL is stored in the database and travels in an export; the vault is the only place a credential belongs.
route.unreadable: could not decide where %q should go: Ferrule could not read its own routing tables, and will not guess
route.unrecordable: Ferrule could not record this request, so it did not make it. The egress ledger is the point of the product; routing traffic it cannot account for would be worse than refusing. Check the config directory is writable: %s
serve.lanListening: Reachable on your network at http://%s/v1
serve.lanNote: Inference only. The control panel stays on this machine — anyone else on the network gets 403 from it, so your vault is not reachable even though the endpoint is.
serve.lanToken: Each person needs their own app token: `ferrule key <name>`. That is what makes the usage and egress views say who did what.
serve.lanCleartext: App tokens cross the network in the clear. On your own wifi that is the same trust boundary every other box on it already sits behind, but a token spends money — so mint one per person and revoke rather than share.
control.notLocal: The control surface is only served to this machine. Ferrule is reachable from %s for inference, but reading the vault, minting tokens and exporting configuration stay here.
ui.grants.lanHint: This machine is on your network. Give whoever this token is for the base URL below — theirs, not localhost.
ui.grants.forThisMachine: For an app on this machine
ui.grants.forOthers: For a machine on your network
